narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: SC judgment on the appeal, or a conciliation settlement whose terms show a steep discount on USD 2.81 bn.

symmetryCheck: Control 1 — Congress-era MoPNG (Deora, Jaipal Reddy, Moily, 2006–14) with the same lens: the PSC that generated the KG-D6 windfall was signed under NDA-I (2000) but the CAG's 2011 findings (area retention, single-bid Aker contract) fault UPA-era ministry conduct, and ONGC's pilferage suit came only in May 2014, RIL's twelfth year of operatorship — so the picture of a ministry deferential to RIL is at least as alarming under Congress as under BJP, and the record of state action against RIL (2015 committee, 2016 demand, 2023 appeal, 2025 DB win, 2026 'theft' submission) is BJP-era. Control 2 — Cairn: the retrospective tax was imposed and enforced under UPA (2012, 2014) and repealed with a ₹7,900 cr refund under NDA (2021–22) after India lost a BIT award; 'favouring a foreign oil major' reads identically to 'complying with an arbitral award', and the same happened for Vodafone. Control 3 — electoral bonds: the largest oil-gas-linked donor to the opposition was Vedanta (₹125 cr to Congress) — the same group that won 7 OALP-IX blocks from the BJP government, which is evidence that big resource groups fund both sides rather than that awards follow money. Conclusion: the lens produces an equally alarming picture for the controls; what discriminates is the documented litigation record, not the donation pattern.
